# Lesson Learned

## Title
Align Batch Size with Runtime Hardware Constraints

## Explanation
The initial code explicitly set a batch size of 512, annotated with the assumption that it was "Optimized for A100 40GB VRAM." However, the actual runtime environment provided a GPU with only ~16GB of VRAM (indicated by the error message `GPU 0 has a total capacity of 15.77 GiB`). This mismatch caused the memory required to store model activations and gradients during the forward pass to exceed the physical device limits, triggering a crash. The fix was to reduce the batch size to 128, lowering the memory footprint to fit within the available hardware capacity.

## Detection
Look for `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory`. The error message typically details the allocation attempt and the actual hardware limits (e.g., `Tried to allocate 46.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 15.77 GiB`). Check for discrepancies between hardware assumptions in comments (e.g., "A100") and the actual environment.
